newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ROMARIO, RONALDO SCORE TWICE AS BRAZIL WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMARIO, RONALDO SCORE TWICE AS BRAZIL WIN.

text.p: Strikers Romario and Ronaldo scored two goals each as world champions Brazil, playing another in a series of matches at home to inferior opposition, beat understrength Chile 4-0 in a friendly on Wednesday.
The win, against a team deprived of its three best players, followed equally pointless victories over Lithuania, Cameroon, Bosnia and Poland.
In addition to having home advantage, Brazil played at full strength while Chile declined to call-up Marcelo Salas, Sebastian Rozental and Ivan Zamorano, their star trio.

Chile, who play eight World Cup qualifiers and the Copa America over the next six months, want to stay on good terms with their foreign clubs. Salas plays for River Plate of Argentina, Rozental for Rangers of Scotland and Zamorano of Italy's Internazionale.
Chile's sole intent was to avoid a hammering but they only managed to keep their goal intact until the eighth minute when Ronaldo, who plays for Spanish club Barcelona, opened the scoring.
Romario, who made his national team comeback this year after a two-year ban imposed by coach Mario Zagallo for lack of enthusiasm, scored his first goal since his return in the 40th minute.
The referee added to Chile's woes by awarding a highly dubious penalty in the 58th minute.
Earlier on Wednesday, FIFA, world soccer's governing body, criticised the growing trend of players trying to deceive referees and labelled it cheating.

Less than 24 hours later, Ronaldo, arguably the world's best player, went crashing down in the penalty area in melodramatic style after an insignificant tug on his shirt by a defender. Ronaldo himself converted the penalty.
Three minutes later, Romario scored to wrap up a win whose only purpose seemed to be to keep the highly critical local media on the team's side.
Brazil - Taffarel, Cafu (Cesar Prates), Aldair, Goncalves, Roberto Carlos, Mauro Silva, Leandro, Juninho, Denilson, Ronaldo (Jardel), Romario.

Chile - Nelson Tapia, Ronald Fuentes, Javier Margas (Raul Munoz), Pedro Reyes, Gabriel Mendoza, Jose Luis Sierra (Jaime Riveros), Mario Salas, Victor Castaneda (Esteban Valencia), Luis Mussri, Claudio Nunez, Ivo Basay (Rodrigo Goldberg).
